meta.title: Muse Wonder: Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI
meta.speakers: Mark Zuckerberg (Meta CEO), Alexandr Wang (Meta Superintelligence Labs), John Collison (host, Stripe)
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · Muse Wonder lands at the frontier · how a frontier model is made · the $100B compute bet · agentic commerce and monetization · personal superintelligence as product · rebooting the lab

snapshot: Meta launches **Muse Wonder** (code name Watermelon), a much bigger pre-train than Muse Spark; Meta says it is state-of-the-art on personal/professional agent, finance and legal evals.
Wonder starts in paid Muse subscriptions, the Meta model API, OpenRouter and Muse Code; the free tier stays on Spark.
The bet: a ~$15B/year cost to run a 1 GW cluster, $50-60B capex per GW, 'tens of billions' per frontier model — CFO Susan Li warned Zuckerberg it 'has to work'.
Zuckerberg's backstop: if AI works, others will rent the compute; for Meta to lose, 'AI overall has to fail'.
Muse is pitched as the first product where people fully delegate purchases; Zuckerberg opened an Instacart account just for his agent and now orders once or twice a week.
MSL is a little over a year old: a full reboot after Llama 4, a research team of ~100-200, a flat culture, and Wang as a first-time frontier-model trainer.
Both reject winner-take-all: uneven execution, distillation and talent choices keep several labs at the frontier.

themes.title: Muse Wonder puts Meta at the frontier — tuned for personal agents, not leaderboards
themes.lead: Meta's new model class is significantly bigger than Muse Spark and built around memory, persistence and domain expertise.
bullets: Two versions: Muse Wonder and the higher-end **Muse Wonder Full** (for Muse Code subscribers); Spark came from a pre-train at the end of 2025.
Active memory: the model itself, not a harness, manages long-term memory and compaction; measured on an internal 'Memory Bench'.
Active focus: persistence on long, ambiguous tasks and finding aligned workarounds when blocked.
Claimed state-of-the-art on finance and legal evals and on two long-horizon coding benchmarks; strong on Terminal Bench 4 and SWE-bench.
Wang says it sits at the frontier alongside Astra and Fable 'by the benchmarks', and is 'the best model in the world' for personal/professional agents.
Against Goodhart's-law benchmaxing worries, 'big model smell': Meta measures the gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance, and says Wonder shows a large step up over Spark.
Too costly to serve free for now; the goal is a Spark-sized model as good as Wonder for hundreds of millions of users.

quote.text: We think it really is the best model in the world for the use case of personal professional agents.

themes.watch: All benchmark claims are Meta's own measurement ('state-of-the-art based on our measurement'); Wang notes 'plenty of room to improve' on memory.

themes.title: How a frontier model gets made: ladders, troughs of sadness and protractors
themes.lead: Wang and Zuckerberg describe a year-plus process where most bets are placed before any proof exists.
bullets: Pre-training climbs a ladder of models each ~4-5x bigger; data is the public internet, books, Meta's proprietary data and heavy image/audio/video for perception.
Domain data (shopping, personal legal, health, tax advice) goes in at pre-training, not just RL; with the internet not growing fast, data is a key scaling constraint.
Post-training: SFT seeds behaviors (maybe 10% of the time), RL drives them up; in RL 'less is more' on data. Spark 1.0 to 1.3 was RL-only yet felt 'night and day'.
Alignment is curating RL environments so the only path to success is aligned behavior; Meta aligns to **the user's instructions and values** — no 'moralizing lecture'.
Discretion matters for personal agents: booking a table without revealing an allergy or pregnancy.
Internal evals now outweigh public ones — chasing viral benchmarks means 'outsourcing all of your product thinking to that PhD student'.
Signals of success: perplexity evals in pre-training; Wonder beat Spark almost immediately in RL. Researchers literally hold protractors to loss curves.
Code names: Avocado (Spark), Watermelon (Wonder) — 'we're out of fruits'.

quote.text: you're kind of outsourcing all of your product thinking to that PhD student who happened to make a viral benchmark

themes.status: HYPERION 5 GW COMING ONLINE OVER A COUPLE OF YEARS
themes.title: The $100-200B bet placed before the cards were dealt
themes.lead: Meta committed to clusters and serving capacity years ahead of knowing whether the model or product would work.
bullets: Rough math: ~$15B a year to operate a gigawatt; $50-60B capex up front per GW; 'tens of billions' to train a frontier model.
Prometheus (Ohio) scales past 1 GW; Hyperion (Louisiana) to 5 GW — both planned in 2023-24 under the Llama program, predating MSL.
Hawaii exec offsite, end of 2025: a '$100 billion or $200 billion' check with no model to show; CFO **Susan Li** repeatedly warned it would be 'very very bad' if it failed.
Zuckerberg's backstop: others would pay more than $15B per GW if AI works, and Meta has other internal uses for compute.
Accounting edge: owned data centers are depreciated over years, while rivals renting cloud pay annual rates; an H100 is worth more today than last year as compute stays constrained.
Wang: R&D overlaps several model generations at once (a point Dario Amodei has made), so spend looks front-loaded.

quote.text: in order for it not to work out it's not just that we have to fail AI overall has to fail

themes.status: STRIPE AGENT COMMERCE WENT VERTICAL IN SEPTEMBER
themes.title: Agents as shoppers: Muse turns delegation into a business model
themes.lead: Meta plans to fund the buildout through subscriptions, a cut of commerce, business agents, an API and an enterprise unit.
bullets: Muse uses trained-in browser use so no business has to integrate; partners get direct APIs, and eventually 'every business is going to have agents'.
Far more businesses ask to integrate than try to block; Collison: thin-moat sites that profit from time-on-site or overcharging may rationally block — and get disrupted.
Zuckerberg opened an **Instacart** account for his Muse (weekend baking with his daughter) and now uses it 1-2x a week — agents may expand commerce's total market by holding accounts.
Collison: Stripe's agent-commerce volume, announced at Sessions in May, went vertical in September; Zuckerberg told Patrick Collison in 2023 he was 'behind the eight-ball'.
Revenue paths: subscriptions, a small cut of money Muse saves or makes users, a 'business in a box' for small businesses, the API, and a new Meta Enterprise platform.
The core ads business — 'hundreds of billions' and growing — funds the rest if models lift it a few percent.
Stripe agreed to acquire OpenRouter (not yet closed); Wang sees it helping developers grasp subtle model differences, a 'wine sommelier' view of models.

themes.title: Personal superintelligence: multimodal, model-is-the-product, no model picker
themes.lead: Meta chose the consumer agent lane others left open, betting on multimodality while the industry obsessed over coding.
bullets: Use cases: Wang's Muse ('Oiler') buys obscure teas from Taiwan and Japan weekly; Zuckerberg's watches gym cameras and gives MMA feedback in 60-second breaks, writing its own video pipeline (first prototyped on OpenClaw, now an internal eval).
'Everyone is actually going to be writing tons of code. They're just not going to know' — Zuckerberg.
Lineage: ChatGPT did the text assistant, Anthropic got coding agents to work; nobody built the personal consumer version. Meta AI remains the informational assistant.
'The model is the product': complex product work is the privacy/security model and a dedicated VM per agent; personality and proactivity are trained in.
No model or effort selector — Wang mocks industry naming where 'the numbers go backwards'.

Voice (Siri-era promise still unmet): turn-taking is hard; input is exploding (students 'word vomit' 10-15 minutes), but listening is slow vs visual; Muse voice mode separates speakers, not fully rolled out.
Hardware: camera-and-audio glasses already useful; small-display glasses shipping; Muse Gadgets (e.g. a USB Home Link controlling Sonos and lights) with phone makers integrating.

quote.text: the highest use of super intelligence is invention and creation not automation

themes.title: Rebooting the lab: talent density, a flat org and a CEO who clears his calendar
themes.lead: After Llama 4, Zuckerberg rebuilt Meta's AI effort around a small elite team led by an outsider who had never trained a frontier model.
bullets: Llama 4 shipped April 4, 2025; ~2 weeks later Zuckerberg started calling for advice. After a 44-minute call, Wang sent a plan whose first point was **talent density**.
Research team under 200, 'closer to 100' plus infra; tens of people per stage vs hundreds elsewhere; compute concentrated per researcher, not 'peanut buttered'.
Collison's four unusual moves: calling the prior effort not good enough, paying 'ungodly amounts' (incl. 49% of Scale AI), betting on Wang, and clearing the CEO calendar for 1-2 months.
The full reboot was decided while recruiting; people came from Llama and FAIR too. One former lead had argued consumers didn't need a reasoning model.
Culture: ~200 direct reports to Wang, no non-technical managers, everyone uses agents and writes code; no deadlines. Wang records his 'insecure overachievers'' pessimistic forecasts and replays them.
Meta leadership got 'AI-pilled' — Instagram's Adam Mosseri runs an advanced personal vibe-code setup; Kunal Shah (founder of CRED) now runs WhatsApp to push commerce in India.
Not winner-take-all: execution varies across labs, distillation is an 'anti-hegemonic force', and many researchers chose labs that serve billions; Zuckerberg sees diversity of models as safer.

quote.text: sometimes you have to reboot a team

themes.watch: Zuckerberg calls it 'a level 10 out of 10 difficulty thing' that is not finished.

takeaways.title: Test Muse Wonder on your own long-horizon tasks — its benchmarks are Meta's own
Expose an API or agent for AI shoppers before blocking them becomes a liability
Model Meta's AI capex at ~$50-60B per GW built and ~$15B per GW-year operated
Keep AI teams small and technical — remove non-technical management layers
Build internal evals around your users instead of chasing public leaderboards

other_news.title: Sources referenced: Patrick Collison's long X post on agentic commerce, a Roon tweet on pre-training ('chew glass'), Dario Amodei on overlapping R&D, third-party reports on Muse growth.
On air, Collison had Muse order a watermelon to Stripe's South San Francisco office; Zuckerberg's Muse had earlier added a watermelon to his baking order on launch weekend.
Zuckerberg on posting: authenticity beats scripting; he cross-posts on Threads, while Wang's prolific X posting is meme-driven. Episode closes over a keg of Guinness from Dublin.

glossary.def: Training a base model on huge volumes of mixed data; the most compute-heavy, highest-stakes stage.
Supervised fine-tuning: showing the model example inputs and desired outputs to seed behaviors.
Reinforcement learning on graded tasks to make desired behaviors reliable.
Meta's metric for real capability: small gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance.
Training a smaller model to mimic a bigger one, packing strong capability into cheaper models.
Few people, each as strong as possible, with lots of compute per researcher.
Meta's term for the model itself managing long-term memory and context compaction.
